channel.title: Pier & Point · Genentech Hall
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Genentech Hall (Mission Bay), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Genentech Hall: On the Genentech Hall timeline, the 2003 opening used to appear…
item.description: On the Genentech Hall timeline, the 2003 opening used to appear twice, from two tables with different wording; it now appears once. Dates and statuses are unchanged and no source was dropped. Source: Pier & Point editorial decision.

item.title: Correction · Genentech Hall: Long 'At a glance' values were cut to the fact itself (or 'Sources…
item.description: Long 'At a glance' values were cut to the fact itself (or 'Sources differ'); the disputes, quoted excerpts and hedging moved to this record's open questions, with every source still named. No change to the record's status or shape. Source: Pier & Point's own text edit.

item.title: Correction · Genentech Hall: Genentech Hall's map notes said it opened in January 2003, while its…
item.description: Genentech Hall's map notes said it opened in January 2003, while its record gave only the year. The notes now give 2003, as UCSF's history page does, and say the month is unconfirmed. Source: A History of UCSF, 1990-2009 (https://history.library.ucsf.edu/1990.html).

item.title: Correction · Genentech Hall: The Genentech Hall page now says it is probably UCSF's first Mission…
item.description: The Genentech Hall page now says it is probably UCSF's first Mission Bay building but that no source names it as such (Gladstone's history says UCSF's first Mission Bay building opened in 2003 without naming it; UCSF's history page lists Genentech Hall in 2003 and Rock Hall in 2004). Its size is given with each source: UCSF's history page says more than 400,000 gross square feet, Clark Construction says 435,000 square feet in its text and 415,000 in its size field, and a January 2000 UC Regents item gave a planned 433,828. The footprint is described as crowd-mapped OpenStreetMap data, not a survey, and the example Assessor lot is the one this building actually lies in. Source: https://history.library.ucsf.edu/1990.html; https://gladstone.org/about/history; https://www.clarkconstruction.com/our-work/projects/ucsf-mission-bay-campus-genentech-hall; https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/regmeet/jan00/3a.pdf.

item.title: Correction · Genentech Hall: Genentech Hall's $222.4 million figure is now described as the…
item.description: Genentech Hall's $222.4 million figure is now described as the estimated project cost the Regents approved a funding plan for in 1999, not as a final cost. Source: https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/regmeet/jan00/3a.pdf.

item.title: Correction · Genentech Hall: Genentech Hall's January 2003 opening month came from a page that…
item.description: Genentech Hall's January 2003 opening month came from a page that could not be re-read; the opening is now dated 2003, as UCSF's own history page gives it. Source: https://history.library.ucsf.edu/1990.html; https://gladstone.org/about/history.

item.title: Correction · Genentech Hall: The '303-acre campus' wording was dropped (that is the whole Mission…
item.description: The '303-acre campus' wording was dropped (that is the whole Mission Bay area; UCSF's history and Clark describe a 43-acre campus), the programs housed now follow UCSF's history page (structural and chemical biology, molecular, cell and developmental biology, the Molecular Design Institute) rather than 'biochemistry, biophysics', and the unsupported 'San Francisco office' for SmithGroup was removed. Size and story-count facts now also cite UCSF's history and Clark. The parcel note now gives 675 Mission Bay Blvd at about 12.2 acres, and a dated note says the tax-roll claim for 600 16th St is unsupported (the parcel is addressed 1700 4th St). The Block 24A/B label now cites UCSF's June 2025 CAC map. The 2008 photo no longer carries a 'taken' date because the source dates only the presentation, and the Wikimedia photo credit no longer names an author or a flight the file page does not state. The January 2003 opening and 'first building' claims rest on a Tradeline article that could not be read and were left in place. Source: A History of UCSF, 1990-2009 (https://history.library.ucsf.edu/1990.html); Clark Construction, UCSF Mission Bay Campus Genentech Hall (https://www.clarkconstruction.com/our-work/projects/ucsf-mission-bay-campus-genentech-hall); UCSF Mission Bay Development Overview, Mission Bay CAC, 2025-06-12 (https://sfocii.org/sites/default/files/2025-06/Item%202%20-%20UCSF%20Mission%20Bay%20Development%20Overview.pdf); DataSF Parcels (https://data.sfgov.org/Geographic-Locations-and-Boundaries/Parcels-Active-and-Retired/acdm-wktn); UC Regents presentation, 2008-09 (https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/regmeet/sept08/j1pp.pdf).
item.source: A History of UCSF, 1990-2009 (https://history.library.ucsf.edu/1990.html); Clark Construction, UCSF Mission Bay Campus Genentech Hall (https://www.clarkconstruction.com/our-work/projects/ucsf-mission-bay-campus-genentech-hall); UCSF Mission Bay Development Overview, Mission Bay CAC, 2025-06-12 (https://sfocii.org/sites/default/files/2025-06/Item%202%20-%20UCSF%20Mission%20Bay%20Development%20Overview.pdf); DataSF Parcels (https://data.sfgov.org/Geographic-Locations-and-Boundaries/Parcels-Active-and-Retired/acdm-wktn); UC Regents presentation, 2008-09 (https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/regmeet/sept08/j1pp.pdf)

item.title: Added · Genentech Hall: The March 1999 UC Regents item approves a $222.4 million…
item.description: The March 1999 UC Regents item approves a $222.4 million capital-improvement budget for 'UC Hall Seismic Replacement, Mission Bay' (Building 24). It is identified as Genentech Hall by matching gross square footage (433,828 gsf) and program to the January 2000 Regents update that recounts the March 1999 action; the 1999 item itself never uses the name 'Genentech Hall', so the match is inferred, not certain. Source: UC Regents, Update on the Development at Mission Bay, San Francisco Campus (joint meeting of the Committees on Grounds and Buildings and on Finance), 2000-01-19 (https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/regmeet/jan00/3a.pdf).
item.source: UC Regents, Update on the Development at Mission Bay, San Francisco Campus (joint meeting of the Committees on Grounds and Buildings and on Finance), 2000-01-19 (https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/regmeet/jan00/3a.pdf)

item.title: Complete · Genentech Hall: Genentech Hall opens, UCSF's first Mission Bay building (UCSF's… (~2003)
item.description: Genentech Hall opens, UCSF's first Mission Bay building (UCSF's history page gives 2003; Gladstone's history says UCSF's first Mission Bay building opened in 2003); the January month rests on a Tradeline page that could not be re-read (~2003). Source: A History of UCSF (UCSF-affiliated historical archive); Gladstone Institutes; Tradeline Inc. (trade press), 2003-02.
item.source: A History of UCSF (UCSF-affiliated historical archive); Gladstone Institutes; Tradeline Inc. (trade press), 2003-02

item.title: Planned · Genentech Hall: UC Regents approve an amendment to the capital-improvement… (Mar 1999)
item.description: UC Regents approve an amendment to the capital-improvement budget and a funding plan for the $222.4 million estimated project cost, and approve the environmental documentation and design, for the 'UC Hall Seismic Replacement, Mission Bay' project (Building 24) – believed to be this building based on matching gross square footage (433,828 gsf) and programs (structural/chemical biology, molecular/cell/developmental biology), per a January 2000 Regents item recounting the March 1999 action; site preparation began October 1999 and steel-frame construction began December 1999, per the same January 2000 item (Mar 1999). Source: The Regents of the University of California, 2000-01.
item.source: The Regents of the University of California, 2000-01
